description: This pie chart visually represents the distribution of media sources cited or referenced in a political discourse narrative, with each slice corresponding to a specific outlet or category and labeled with its proportional value. The chart is divided into 15 distinct segments, each with a unique color and numerical label indicating its share of the total. The largest segment is “Breitbart” at 14%, followed by “Other” at 13%, and “Drudge Report” at 8%. “The Daily Caller” also accounts for 8%. Other notable slices include “NPR” and “The Huffington Post” at 7%, “Vox” and “The Guardian” at 6%, “BBC” and “RT” at 5%, and several smaller segments such as “Daily Kos,” “National Review,” “Red State,” “Fox News,” “CNN,” “Shareblue,” and “PoliticusUSA,” each at 3%. The chart includes a legend implicitly through the labeled slices and uses distinct colors to differentiate each source. Percentage values are explicitly labeled within each slice, and no segments appear to be visually emphasized through explosion or bolding. The segments are arranged in a clockwise descending order of size, starting from the largest slice at the top right (“Breitbart”).
